narrative.overview:
The popup is an anime game character messenger (角色通讯). The companion lends her face and image colour (印象色) to the interface: a bright gradient header, manga screentone, rounded dialogue bubbles and pill controls. Her rig portrait looks away while thinking and moves its mouth while replying.

This system governs the embedded chat and settings popup, not the hosted site or the pet’s speech bubble. It remains browser-only, with local system fonts and inline SVG artwork; no external font or portrait asset is required. Dark mode follows the device preference and uses character-tinted night surfaces.
keyCharacteristics: Character identity comes from her rig and image colour.
A gradient, screentone dots and slanted stripes distinguish the header.
Companion bubbles use the input surface; user bubbles use the character fill and white text.
Round portraits, pill actions and four-point sparkles repeat across chat and settings.

rules.name: The Page and Character Colour Rule
rules.body: Prefer host theme tokens, matching theme-color metadata, then visible filled controls; use coloured backgrounds and styled links as secondary signals. Map to the seven contrast-tested gradient families. Ignore neutral or nearly transparent colours and default browser links. Resample on open, host theme changes and resize with bounded work, never on scroll. Without a usable page accent, use the character mapping, palette hue, then deterministic id fallback. Late portraits cannot override a page colour; artwork retains its original palette.

rules.name: The Fill and Accent Rule
rules.body: Use character colour for filled controls and user bubbles. Use the derived accent for links, focus and sparkles; dark mode takes the character’s light tone for that accent.

rules.name: The Local Font Rule
rules.body: Use only the implemented local font stacks. Rounded headings are a platform-constrained fallback, not a portable display-face recommendation for other surfaces.

rules.name: The Mobile Sixteen Rule
rules.body: At host viewport widths of 480px and below, text inputs and the composer use 16px text; icon and tab targets grow to at least 44px.

dos: Do carry character identity through portraits, gradient stops, bubble fills and active controls.
Do keep rig portraits decorative and retain textual names, model status and accessible control labels.
Do retain visible focus outlines and device-driven light, dark and reduced-motion behaviour.
Do use four-point CSS or SVG sparkles for the empty portrait surround, memory markers and decorative fallback.
donts: Don't hash bundled characters to arbitrary colours; keep their hand-mapped image colours.
Don't load external fonts, portrait images or icon fonts into the embedded popup.
Don't replace the character’s face with invented raster artwork when her rig portrait is available.
